pattern: face numbering differs from OpenCascade's
evidence: A pure permutation: Rust numbers the CLOSED_SHELL's faces in file order (#17, #145, #216, ...); Python's face i is read from #17, #216, #752, #1166, ... (specify_core.requirements.face_entities_of), the order OpenCascade's reader gives (why it departs from the file's order was not established). Each face's kind, area and centroid agree entity for entity (Python's face 1 = #216 = Rust's face 2: plane, 343.078). An analysis of this file must not cross engines (question Q1); which order is 'right' is a convention.

pattern: step_levels: no such family in quiddity-rust
evidence: Produced by Python quiddity's cross-family reconciliation (build_recognition_result), which quiddity-rust does not port (features/mod.rs: 'the Python aggregate's cross-family reconciliation is not ported'; U2). Rust's analysis lacks the feature Python reports (upstream need U12); specify-core's rules read only holes, hole_patterns and turned_steps, so no question changes, but the picker's feature list does.

pattern: a section recess Python lists is missing in Rust
evidence: Since v0.1.0-alpha.2 quiddity-rust publishes section_recesses in Features, but not as Python does: Python's evidence view lists refused regions (record with a reason, e.g. unsupported_support_geometry) as features, which quiddity-rust carries as refusals in its recognition document, not in Features. (Since 0.1.0-alpha.4 quiddity-rust also takes Python's local-degradation retry, so 13975 and 14052 match Python.) Upstream need U12; specify-core's rules read only holes, hole_patterns and turned_steps, so no question changes, but the picker's feature list does.

pattern: risers: no such family in quiddity-rust
evidence: quiddity-rust has recognise_risers, but outside Features ('measurements with no evidence path yet', features/mod.rs), so recognise does not return them. Rust's analysis lacks the feature Python reports (upstream need U12); specify-core's rules read only holes, hole_patterns and turned_steps, so no question changes, but the picker's feature list does.

pattern: a drilled hole's point cone is constituent, not defining
evidence: Every such hole's record has bottom 'drill_point': Python's faces add the drill-point cone to the bore. quiddity-rust gives defining faces only (Features::defining); Python quiddity's evidence view gives constituent faces (upstream need U2).

pattern: a pattern's member holes lack their drill-point cones
evidence: The members are drill-point holes (bottom 'drill_point'); the pattern's faces are its members'. quiddity-rust gives defining faces only (Features::defining); Python quiddity's evidence view gives constituent faces (upstream need U2).

pattern: a blind hole's floor is constituent, not defining
evidence: Every such hole's record has bottom 'flat': Python's faces add the floor plane. quiddity-rust gives defining faces only (Features::defining); Python quiddity's evidence view gives constituent faces (upstream need U2).

pattern: a pattern's blind member holes lack their floors
evidence: As for the member holes (bottom 'flat'). quiddity-rust gives defining faces only (Features::defining); Python quiddity's evidence view gives constituent faces (upstream need U2).

pattern: a blind hole's freeform floor is constituent, not defining
evidence: Record bottom 'flat'; face 126 is the floor (kind other). quiddity-rust gives defining faces only (Features::defining); Python quiddity's evidence view gives constituent faces (upstream need U2).

pattern: a polygonal boss's end face is constituent, not defining
evidence: Records equal; Python's extra plane is the boss's top, its normal along the record's axis (NIST CTC-01 face 104, +z, top 50; FTC-07 faces 236 and 265, -y). quiddity-rust gives defining faces only (Features::defining); Python quiddity's evidence view gives constituent faces (upstream need U2). Resolved by quiddity #57/#61 at v0.1.1: Framed defining support is now compared as separate family:faces IDs, rather than a constituent end-plane difference; the new polygonal-boss entries retain the old/new supports. This retained entry asserts absence; any returning departure fails even if another active entry matches it.

pattern: a boss's end face is constituent, not defining

pattern: an angled step's adjoining plane is constituent, not defining
evidence: Records equal; Python's faces add a plane. quiddity-rust gives defining faces only (Features::defining); Python quiddity's evidence view gives constituent faces (upstream need U2).

pattern: a section recess's plane is constituent, not defining

pattern: thin wall body: Python lists more faces

Not settled which side is right until the oracle is recaptured with quiddity 0.4. Resolved by quiddity #57/#61 at v0.1.1: The old coplanar-face deficit on risers:4 is absent. Its current local level/envelope differences are recorded separately with frame metadata, not hidden as face changes. This retained entry asserts absence; any returning departure fails even if another active entry matches it.

evidence: A difference of 1e-7 mm: the face's plane is at z = -40 in the STEP file; Python's value carries OpenCascade's tolerance noise, Rust's is the plane's exact height.

pattern: a measured modelled screw thread replaces its blanket freeform classification
evidence: Independently checked on 2026-10-20 with OpenCascade (~/cld/quiddity/.venv/bin/python -I tools/known_differences/threads.py INPUT ANALYSIS), reading the original STEP and Specify analyse output as hypotheses; no quiddity recogniser is imported. All 16 flank patches belong to the same external helical thread: independently fitted OCP boundary leads 6.3500357813..6.3500357815 mm with maximum axial residual 0.000101603 mm (6.35 mm reported pitch, one start, right hand). Crest radii 54.96944734..55.00543695 mm and root radii 51.55998189..51.56512027 mm agree with the reported major 109.99979735 and minor 103.12000000 mm within the stated diameter bounds. Flank/runout bounds independently give Z 367.61420731113..419.20579270186 mm, matching the measured span rather than the carrier length. The 136 old B-spline freeform records (flanks, crests, root strips and runouts) become faces of one measured thread; four unrelated freeforms remain and every original face remains in the analysis. The regression modelled_thread_parts_still_analyse_interview_and_write checks the counts, interview, nonempty intent, verified write and resumed answers. OCP local differential leads vary (6.02479..6.67995 mm), and nearly collapsed root strips have ambiguous normals; the evidence is for global pitch, dimensions and physical-thread classification, not certified continuous spline bounds or a nominal thread standard.

All 16 flank patches belong to the same external helical thread: independently fitted OCP boundary leads 6.3500357813..6.3500357815 mm with maximum axial residual 0.000101603 mm (6.35 mm reported pitch, one start, right hand). Crest radii 54.96944734..55.00543695 mm and root radii 51.55998189..51.56512027 mm agree with the reported major 109.99979735 and minor 103.12000000 mm within the stated diameter bounds. Flank/runout bounds independently give Z 367.61420731113..419.20579270186 mm, matching the measured span rather than the carrier length. The 136 old B-spline freeform records (flanks, crests, root strips and runouts) become faces of one measured thread; four unrelated freeforms remain and every original face remains in the analysis. The regression modelled_thread_parts_still_analyse_interview_and_write checks the counts, interview, nonempty intent, verified write and resumed answers. OCP local differential leads vary (6.02479..6.67995 mm), and nearly collapsed root strips have ambiguous normals; the evidence is for global pitch, dimensions and physical-thread classification, not certified continuous spline bounds or a nominal thread standard.
